title: Already happened
description: Say what has already happened today.
grammar: el pretérito perfecto, he + the participle
grammarNote: The perfect is he + the participle: he hablado, has comido, hemos visto.

explanation.summary: The preterite perfect joins the preterite of haber with the participle of the main verb. It says something has happened and it still matters now, usually because it happened today.

sections.heading: How it is built
sections.body: He, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han, followed by the participle. The participle of -ar verbs ends in -ado: hablar, hablado. Of -er and -ir verbs it ends in -ido: comer, comido; vivir, vivido. The eight irregular verbs have irregular participles: escrito, hecho, dicho, puesto, abierto, visto, resuelto, vuelto.

examples.en: I have spoken to the teacher.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.body: The perfect is for the past with a link to now: this morning, today, this week, already, yet. The preterite is for a finished time: yesterday, last year, in 2020. Spanish is stricter about this than English, which often uses the perfect for things with a finished time too.

examples.en: I have finished the work today.

sections.heading: The negative
sections.body: No he comido means I have not eaten, and it is the normal way to say you have not eaten yet. With the preterite, no comí says you did not eat, which sounds more like you skipped a meal on purpose.

examples.en: I have not seen the film.

drills.note: The perfect for something that happened today.
Ayer takes the preterite, but the auxiliary is still he.
